{{ Cross-country skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics}}
The '''men's sprint''' competition in [[Cross-country skiing at the 2026 Winter Olympics|cross-country skiing]] at the [[2026 Winter Olympics]] was held on 10 February,<!-- 2026--> over a {{convert|1.585|km|adj=on}} course<ref>{{cite news |first=Marisa |last=Marcellino |title=Cross-Country Skiing 101: Competition format |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=2025-08-10 |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/cross-country-skiing-101-competition-format |access-date=2026-02-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821130205/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/cross-country-skiing-101-competition-format |archive-date=2025-08-21 |url-status=live}}</ref> at the [[Cross country and biathlon center Fabio Canal]] in [[Tesero]].<ref name=schedule>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/schedule/ccs|title=2026 Olympic Winter Games Competition Schedule Version - Cross-country skiing|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref> [[Johannes Høsflot Klæbo]] of Norway, the 2018 and 2022 champion, won the event and his seventh gold medal. [[Ben Ogden]] of the United States won silver, and [[Oskar Opstad Vike]] won bronze.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/crosscountry-klaebo-clinches-seventh-gold-mens-classic-sprint-2026-02-10/|title=Crosscountry-Klaebo cruises to seventh gold in men's classic sprint|publisher=Reuters|accessdate=28 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/ben-ogden-ends-united-states-50-year-medal-drought-cross-country-silver-sprint|title=Ben Ogden ends 50-year cross-country medal drought for U.S. men; Klaebo gold in sprint|publisher=NBC Olympics|accessdate=28 February 2026}}</ref> Both became the first-time medalists. Ogden became the first American male cross-country skier to win a medal since [[Bill Koch (skier)|Bill Koch]] in 1976.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eu.burlingtonfreepress.com/story/sports/2026/02/10/vermont-ben-ogden-olympics-silver-medal-mens-cross-country-sprint/88603829007/|title=Vermont's Ben Ogden wins cross-country skiing silver to end USA Olympic medal drought|publisher=Burlington Free Press|accessdate=28 February 2026}}</ref>

==Background==
The 2022 champion, [[Johannes Høsflot Klæbo]], qualified for the Olympics, as did the silver medalist, [[Federico Pellegrino]]. The bronze medalist, [[Alexander Terentyev]], was barred from participation because skiers from Russia could only participate as [[Individual Neutral Athletes at the 2026 Winter Olympics|individual neutral athletes]], and he did not obtain this status. Klæbo was leading both overall and sprint standings of the [[2025–26 FIS Cross-Country World Cup]] before the Olympics. He was the [[FIS Nordic World Ski Championships 2025 – Men's sprint|2025 world champion]] in sprint as well.

===Semifinals===
Two fastest athletes from each semifinal qualified (Q) for the final. In addition, two athletes with the fastest times among all others ("lucky losers", LL) also qualified.
